AUDIT: FAIL
Objective Understood: Reviewed worker task 'sweep-adopt-veridian-scripts-416-fix-dispatch-land-next-queued-task-stale' (risk tier: tier1) by reading the actual diff, not a self-report.
Standards Reviewed: AGENTS.md Operating Rule 7c structured audit protocol; risk-tier.py's deterministic tier classification.
Scope Confirmed:  dispatch-tick.py                                   | 115 +++++++++-
 resource_governor.py                               |  31 ++-
 tests/test_ocid_evidence_supersession.py           |  19 +-
 .../test_resume_stale_task_flagged_not_replayed.py | 253 +++++++++++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 411 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)
Evidence Recorded: The dispatch-tick.py resume-staleness gate is sound and well-tested (3 dedicated tests covering the stale-flag, fresh-resume, and fail-open-no-timestamp paths), but the resource_governor.py change to next_queued_task() introduces a verified permanent-starvation defect for any queued row that crosses MAX_QUEUED_AGE_SECONDS (4h): age is computed from the immutable ts_submitted and only grows, so once a row is skipped for staleness it is skipped on every subsequent tick forever, and the function's own docstring claim that 'a real PM decision (resolve_pm_decision_pending() on its open STALE-QUEUED row)' is what makes it 'eligible again' is false as implemented -- resolving that PM decision never touches the umr_tasks row. Worse, submit()'s pre-existing duplicate-rejection check (find_active_umr_by_identity) treats status='queued' as active, so a fresh resubmission of the same task_identity is rejected as a duplicate for as long as the stale row sits queued, i.e. indefinitely -- the only real recovery path is a human noticing the STALE-QUEUED-AGGREGATE decision and separately running resource_governor.py --stop-task/--delete-task via the CLI before resubmitting, which the code comments never state. This is a real, live-affecting change to the core dispatch-selection path used every tick for every queued task system-wide, and it ships with zero dedicated unit test of its own (the only touched test, test_ocid_evidence_supersession.py, was patched merely to dodge the new gate, not to verify it) -- a sharp asymmetry against the thorough coverage given to the narrower dispatch-tick.py path. No .github/workflows/** files are touched, so the hard workflow-push rule is not implicated. Issues found: resource_governor.py next_queued_task(): a queued row that crosses MAX_QUEUED_AGE_SECONDS is skipped on every tick forever (age is measured from immutable ts_submitted, which only increases) -- there is no code path anywhere in this diff or the surrounding module that resets ts_submitted or moves the row out of status='queued' once flagged, so the row never becomes selectable again through any automated mechanism.; next_queued_task()'s own added docstring asserts resolving the row's STALE-QUEUED pm_decisions_pending entry (resolve_pm_decision_pending()) is what returns it to eligibility -- that is not implemented; resolving the PM decision has zero effect on the umr_tasks row's status or ts_submitted, so the comment is actively misleading to whoever handles that decision.; Because submit()'s find_active_umr_by_identity() dedup check treats status='queued' as active, a human cannot even work around the stuck row by resubmitting the same task_identity -- it will be rejected as rejected_duplicate for as long as the stale row remains queued. The only real recovery is a human manually running resource_governor.py --stop-task or --delete-task on the old row first, which is undocumented in this diff.; No dedicated unit test exercises next_queued_task()'s new stale-skip behavior directly (e.g. stale row is skipped while a fresher lower-priority row is still selected; all-rows-stale returns None; the permanent-skip/no-recovery behavior). The one test touched for this area (test_ocid_evidence_supersession.py) only adjusts a timestamp to avoid tripping the new gate, it does not verify the gate's own behavior.
Severity Classified: medium
Verdict: fail
Corrective Action Owner: Worker to address the findings listed above and resubmit.
Re-Audit Scheduled: Required after corrective changes are pushed.
